This means that a person needs to inherit two copies of the mutated gene, one from each parent, to develop the condition. If a person inherits only one copy of the mutated gene, they are usually carriers and may not display symptoms but can pass the gene to their offspring.

However, in some cases, polymicrogyria can be caused by mutations in genes that are not inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern, but rather in an autosomal dominant pattern. In these cases, a single copy of the mutated gene is enough to cause the condition.

It's worth noting that the exact genetic cause of polymicrogyria is not yet fully understood, and more research is needed to determine the specific genetic factors
